data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘Fitr’, which signifies the natural disposition or inherent qualities that humans are born with, before being influenced by external factors. In Islam, Fitrah refers to the inherent belief in monotheism and the submission to God, which is present in every human being. The name Fitrah carries the meaning “Pure Nature, Innate Disposition” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fitrah usually hope their child will grow to embody pure nature, innate disposition and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Muslims around the world come together to perform the Eid prayer and engage in acts of charity, emphasizing the unity of spirit and the common thread of human nature that connects us all.

By adhering to our Fitrah and nurturing our inherent beliefs in monotheism and submission to God, we are able to build a strong spiritual foundation and deepen our connection with the divine. This concept also underlines the importance of personal responsibility in our spiritual journey, as we are guided by our own conscience, rather than relying on external sources or external influence. Fitrah serves as a reminder of our ultimate purpose in life and encourages us to constantly strive towards self-improvement and closeness to God.
